label: Regulatory Risk Assessment for Startups
description: Pragmatic, stage-appropriate regulatory-risk assessment for founders: licensing perimeter, data and privacy, sector-specific rules (fintech, health, AI), the real cost of getting it wrong, and a risk-prioritised compliance roadmap proportionate to your stage and runway.

claudeKnowledge.description: EU and national regulatory instruments relevant to early-stage companies: GDPR (EU) 2016/679, the EU AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, the AMLR (EU) 2024/1624 / AMLD6 (EU) 2024/1640 / AMLA Reg (EU) 2024/1620 package, MiCA (EU) 2023/1114, EMD2 2009/110/EC, PSD2 2015/2366, the Transfer of Funds Regulation (EU) 2023/1113, DORA (EU) 2022/2554, the Medical Devices Regulation (EU) 2017/745, the Digital Services Act (EU) 2022/2065, the Digital Markets Act (EU) 2022/1925, consumer-protection directives, and national licensing regimes. Supplement with current supervisory guidance via web search when in-force dates or transitional periods are decisive.

guidedInputs.label: Core Business Model
guidedInputs.description: What does the startup actually do? This determines which regulatory perimeters can be triggered.

options.label: AI / ML product (model, agent, or AI-enabled SaaS)
B2B / B2C SaaS handling personal or sensitive data

guidedInputs.label: Company Stage
guidedInputs.description: Stage sets the proportionality bar — how much compliance is enough right now versus what can wait.

options.label: Series A — scaling, raising institutional capital

guidedInputs.label: Markets / Jurisdictions
guidedInputs.description: Where are the customers, the users, and the company established? Drives which regimes have territorial reach.

guidedInputs.label: Data & Technology Profile
guidedInputs.description: Select everything the product collects, processes, or relies on — each item can pull in a distinct regime.

options.label: Third-party LLMs / foundation models / external APIs

guidedInputs.label: Runway / Risk Appetite
guidedInputs.description: How much room is there to invest in compliance now? Shapes how aggressively we sequence the roadmap.

options.label: Targeting a regulated market — compliance is the moat

guidedInputs.label: Known Concerns or Specific Questions
guidedInputs.description: Describe what worries you, what an investor flagged in diligence, or any specific 'are we allowed to do this?' questions.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. We hold customer funds in a pooled account before paying out merchants — do we need an e-money or payment licence? Investor diligence flagged that we have no DPA with our LLM provider and no record of processing. We market a symptom-checker as 'not a medical device' — is that defensible?

exampleInput: We are a pre-seed Swedish startup (4 founders, no revenue yet) building an AI-powered personal-finance app for EU consumers. The app connects to users' bank accounts via an open-banking aggregator, categorises spending with an LLM, and will later let users move money between their own accounts and round up purchases into a savings pot we hold. We process transaction history and want to add a 'financial coach' that nudges users. We are raising a EUR 1.5M seed round in 6 months and an investor has asked for a regulatory-risk summary. Assess our regulatory perimeter (do we need a payment or e-money licence? are we a credit intermediary?), our GDPR and EU AI Act exposure given the LLM and the automated nudges, the realistic cost of getting licensing wrong, and give us a stage-appropriate compliance roadmap we can actually afford before the raise.

exampleValues.known_concerns: We will hold user savings in a pooled 'round-up' pot before sweeping to their account — unsure if this triggers an e-money or payment-services licence. We use a third-party LLM to categorise transactions and generate financial nudges, with no DPA and no AI Act analysis done. Investor diligence wants a one-page regulatory-risk view before the seed round.
